title: High school football: Top games for Week 4 in the San Antonio area - NewsBreak
text:
By David Hinojosa ,
8 hours ago Steele's Jonathan Hatton looks for running room versus Austin Westlake during a game Sept. 20, 2024, at Lehnhoff Stadium in Schertz. Hatton and the Knights travel to Westlake on Friday for one of the area's top high school football games this week. (Robin Jerstad) While Brennan and Harlan battle it out for the early lead in the District 28-6A race in the Express-News Game of the Week , here’s a rundown of some other notable games in Week 4.
Top games Steele at Austin Westlake 7 p.m. Friday: Steele seeks a program-defining victory on the road against powerhouse Austin Westlake in a battle of state-ranked teams. The Knights (3-0), ranked No. 15 in Class 6A in the Dave Campbell's Texas Football rankings, hasn’t defeated No. 13 Westlake in their last four meetings and is 2-4 all-time against the Chapparals. The Knights are led by senior Jonathan Hatton, a Texas A&M pledge who has rushed for 448 yards and seven touchdowns on 62 carries. Since opening the season with a 29-22 loss against No. 12 Prosper, the Chaps defeated San Benito (66-0) and No. 14 Humble Atascocita 35-28. Westlake is led by senior quarterback and Ole Miss pledge Rees Wise, who has passed for 540 yards and three touchdowns.
HS SCOREBOARD: Check out this weekend's high school football schedule
Smithson Valley vs. Boerne Champion 7 p.m. Friday, Boerne ISD Stadium : Smithson Valley (2-1), listed No. 3 in the Dave Campbell's Class 5A Division I state rankings, begins District 13-5A-I play coming off a 42-10 victory against Madison. Junior quarterback Ty Knutson, who has thrown for 459 yards and three touchdowns on 30-of-47 passing, leads the Rangers along with junior running back Caleb Peagler, who has 224 yards and seven touchdowns on 36 carries. Senior linebacker Colton Hornsby has a team-best five sacks. Boerne Champion (2-1) is coming off a 35-28 loss against Laredo Alexander and is led by junior quarterback Julian Navarrete’s 752 passing yards with nine touchdowns and one interception. Smithson Valley has won all three meetings in their series.
Smithson Valley's Ty Knutson (2) runs past Brennan’s Tyett Morris (9) during the second half of their high school football game at Gustafson Stadium in San Antonio, Thursday, Sept. 4, 2025. Knutson has had a fast start in his first season as the starting quarterback and looks to keep it going this weekend against Boerne Champion. (Marvin Pfeiffer/San Antonio Express-News) Jay at Southwest Legacy 7 p.m. Thursday : Jay (3-0), listed No. 9 in the Express-News Class 6A-5A area rankings, seeks its third straight 4-0 start. The Mustangs are led by sophomore running backs Brennan Oliver (340 rushing yards) and Miles Gutierrez (159 yards). Jay pinned a 15-0 victory against South San last week. Legacy (3-0) is led by junior quarterback Aiden Garcia’s 366 yards and three touchdowns passing. A pair of running backs, senior James Ross (200 yards, three touchdowns) and sophomore Joshua Fontenette (190 yards, four touchdowns), lead the ground game. Jay defeated Legacy 9-3 last season in their only meeting.
Alamo Heights vs. Clemens 7 p.m. Thursday, Lehnhoff Stadium : Alamo Heights (3-0), listed No. 8 in the Dave Campbell's Class 5A Division II state rankings, closes non-district play aiming to extend its regular season winning streak to 33 games. The Mules defeated New Braunfels Canyon 42-20 behind DK Garza’s 298 yards and two touchdowns rushing. The Buffaloes (2-1) opened with a 17-14 loss against Taft and have since defeated Del Valle (39-20) and Churchill (40-17). The Buffaloes have a 13-9-1 advantage in their series, but Alamo Heights has won the last seven meetings. Clemens’ last victory against the Mules occurred in 1978.

Under the radar game Jourdanton at Somerset 7 p.m. Friday: Somerset (2-1), listed No. 7 in the Express-News Sub-5A area rankings, seeks its fourth victory against No. 6 Jourdanton (2-1) with quarterback Kaleb Flores (540 yards, eight touchdowns) and receiver Malakai Iverson (15 catches for 304 yards and six touchdowns). The Bulldogs responded to a 22-10 defeat against McCollum with a 42-14 win against Jefferson last week. Jourdanton, which hasn’t defeated Somerset since 1989, has wins against Devine (50-47) and Pleasanton (22-7) since starting with a 20-19 loss against Poth.
